cases.question: HCP-500 is showing P-07. What does that mean and what should I check first?

segments.text: P-07 means cavitation on the HCP-500.
For HCP-500, the first measure is not the same as on HCP-350, and the strainer threshold is different, so use the HCP-500 fault row for your model.
Check the strainer differential pressure at PI-01/PI-02 first; if it is above 0.30 bar, clean the strainer.
Then confirm the suction isolation valve is fully open.

p_6c8fc0d0ac8ddb694c32ce3e.title: Pump Troubleshooting Playbook
p_6c8fc0d0ac8ddb694c32ce3e.text_original:
Gravel noise and P-07 (cavitation)
If it sounds like someone poured gravel into the pump, it's cavitation. The liquid is boiling at the impeller inlet because the pressure there is too low, and the bubbles collapse against the impeller. Left alone it pits the impeller inlet and you'll be replacing it. The PC-3 flags it as P-07 when the suction pressure starts fluctuating.
Use the P-07 row in the fault table for the model you're on, and read the whole row . The first measure on the HCP-500 isn't the same as on the HCP-350, and the strainer threshold is different between them. People who've worked mostly on 350s get this wrong on the 500s.
What actually causes it at our sites:
Strainer loaded. The usual one. Fresno gets label scraps and bits of shrink film into the return water. Clean the basket, check the mesh for tears (18-1120), new cover gasket (18-1121) every time.
Suction valve not fully open. Somebody did work on the line, reopened the valve by feel, and left it partly closed. A partly closed suction valve looks fine from a distance. Count the turns or check the position indicator.
Tank level low. Ask the operator what level they've been running at. Less liquid above the pump means less pressure at the inlet.
Warm liquid. Hot summer days at Fresno raise the water temperature in the return tank, and warmer water cavitates sooner. If P-07 only happens on hot afternoons, that's your clue. It's still worth cleaning the strainer, because it gives you margin.
FRS-P-0033 (HCP-500) in August 2026 had two of these at once: the strainer was loaded and the suction valve had been left three-quarters open after pipework changes. Cleaning the strainer alone would have brought it back in a week. Case 00043015 if you want the details.
After cleaning, confirm the strainer differential has dropped back to near zero (the manual gives the clean value) before you leave.

cases.question: What's the impeller-to-casing clearance spec on an HCP-200?

segments.text: For an HCP-200, the impeller-to-casing clearance spec is 0.38 - 0.50 mm diametral, per the HCP-200 technical data table.
To check it, measure the clearance between the impeller and wear ring with a feeler gauge at four points 90° apart, and renew the wear rings if the clearance exceeds the maximum in table 3.1.
There is no bulletin change for HCP-200 here; the bulletin says HCP-200 pumps are not affected.

cases.question: How often do I change the oil on a VRS-75?

segments.text: For a VRS-75, change the oil every 6,000 running hours or 12 months, whichever comes first, when you use Vastra SynLube 46.
With mineral compressor oil ISO VG 46, the interval stays 4,000 running hours or 12 months, whichever comes first; the longer 6,000-hour interval is valid only with genuine Vastra SynLube 46.
On compressors delivered before April 2026, the controller is set to 4,000 h from the factory, so you must change the interval manually when you use Vastra SynLube 46.
A service record for FRS-C-0101 shows the oil was changed at 4,000 h, and another record for the same unit shows a 4,000H oil change with SynLube 46 at 23,922 run hours.

What's new in Rev C
This revision replaces Rev B of February 2024. Text that is changed or new compared with Rev B is marked with a vertical bar in the left margin, as for this paragraph.
Longer oil change interval with Vastra SynLube 46: 6,000 running hours or 12 months, whichever comes first. With mineral compressor oil ISO VG 46 the interval is unchanged, 4,000 running hours or 12 months. See 4.1 and 4.2.
On compressors delivered before April 2026 the oil interval in the controller is set to 4,000 h from the factory. The interval must be changed manually when Vastra SynLube 46 is used. See 3.4.
The oil filter is now delivered as part no. 41-1475. It is the same filter as 41-1470 in new packaging. See 4.3 and 6.2.
New warning E-27, separator differential pressure high (above 1.0 bar). Replace the separator element 41-3075 and check the oil carry-over. See 5.1 and 5.2.4.

4.2 Oil
Vastra recommends Vastra SynLube 46 (synthetic, part no. 41-0046, 20 l can). It is allowed to use a mineral compressor oil ISO VG 46 according to DIN 51506 VDL in normal operating conditions. The oil change interval depends on the oil type, see 4.1. The longer interval for Vastra SynLube 46 is based on oil analysis from field installations 2022 - 2025 and is valid only with genuine Vastra SynLube 46.
Do not mix oils of different types or makes. When changing from mineral oil to Vastra SynLube 46, drain the system completely, replace the oil filter, run the compressor for 24 hours and then change the oil and the oil filter a second time.
Control the oil level with the compressor stopped for 2 minutes. The level shall be in the upper half of the sight glass. Top up only with the same oil type. An oil consumption of more than 0.5 l per 100 running hours is not normal; see 5.2.4 and 5.2.5.

p_32f5ef652cfa89ebd0e95aaf.title: Halden SB-2025-009
p_32f5ef652cfa89ebd0e95aaf.text_original:
1 Summary  /  Zusammenfassung
Since production week 01/2024 (serial number HCP350-240001), HCP-350 pumps are built with a revised casing cover and a thinner casing gasket. The tightening torque for the casing bolts on these pumps is 38 N-m, applied in a cross pattern in two passes. The value of 45 N-m given in the Installation, Operation and Maintenance Manual HDN-IOM-350 Rev D applies only to pumps with serial numbers before HCP350-240001.
Tightening a revised casing cover to 45 N-m overloads the gasket seat and can crack it. A cracked gasket seat cannot be repaired. Pumps in service whose casing joint has been opened since delivery must be inspected as described in 5.2.

p_847ef722d1030c3589bfcc13.title: Halden SB-2025-009
p_847ef722d1030c3589bfcc13.text_original:
4 Root cause  /  Ursache
The Version 2 casing cover was introduced to reduce casting weight and to improve casting yield at the foundry. The gasket seat was narrowed and the casing gasket changed from 1.5 mm fibre to 0.8 mm aramid fibre with graphite facing. Pumps are assembled in the factory with 38 N-m. The change was released in production without a corresponding revision of the operating instructions, so the IOM still states 45 N-m in sections 4.3, 8.4 and 8.7.
With the thinner gasket and the narrower seat, a bolt torque of 45 N-m produces a surface pressure on the seat above the permissible value for the casting. The overload alone does not always cause immediate leakage. Cracks initiate at the bolt holes and grow with each heating and cooling cycle. Use of impact wrenches or tightening without a cross pattern increases the risk further.
Halden regrets that the documentation did not follow the production change. The IOM will be corrected in Rev E (see 7).

p_56831c217e16f7d0f8aa12da.title: Halden SB-2025-009
p_56831c217e16f7d0f8aa12da.text_original:
5 Corrective action  /  Massnahmen
5.1  Every time the casing joint of an affected pump is closed
1. Read the pump serial number and check the cast mark on the cover (see 2). Treat any Version 2 cover as affected.
2. Clean the gasket seat on casing and cover. With the gasket removed, inspect the seat for cracks, preferably with dye penetrant. A cracked cover must be replaced (5.2, step 5).
3. Fit a new Version 2 casing gasket. Never reuse a gasket. Never fit a 1.5 mm Version 1 gasket on a Version 2 seat, or the reverse; the joint will not seal.
4. Lightly oil the bolt threads (property class 8.8). Do not use anti-seize paste with a lower friction value; it raises the clamping force at the same torque.
5. Tighten the casing bolts in a cross pattern in two passes: first pass to approximately 20 N-m, second pass to 38 N-m. Use a calibrated torque wrench. Impact tools are not permitted on this joint.
6. After the first 24 hours at operating temperature, check the torque once at 38 N-m. Do not re-tighten beyond this value to stop a leak; a joint that leaks at 38 N-m has a damaged gasket or seat.
7. Record the torque applied and the reference "SB-2025-009" in the maintenance record (IOM Annex B).
5.2  Field inspection of affected pumps in service
Carry out this inspection at the next scheduled maintenance visit, at the latest by 2025-12-31, on all pumps from serial HCP350-240001 (and on earlier pumps fitted with a Version 2 cover) whose casing joint has been opened since delivery. Pumps whose casing joint has never been opened were assembled at the correct torque and need no action.
1. Check the maintenance records for the pump: was the casing joint opened, and which torque was applied? If the records do not state the torque, assume 45 N-m.
2. With the pump running at operating pressure and temperature, inspect the casing joint all round for weeping, glycol or mineral residue, and staining on the casing below the joint.
3. No leakage and 38 N-m documented: no further action. Record the inspection.
4. No leakage but 45 N-m documented or torque unknown: at a convenient stop, isolate and drain the pump (IOM 2.4), slacken the casing bolts, and re-tighten to 38 N-m per 5.1, step 5. Inspect again after 24 hours at operating temperature. If leakage appears, continue with step 5.
5. Leakage present: stop, isolate and drain the pump. Open the casing joint, remove the gasket and inspect the gasket seat with dye penetrant. Without cracks: fit a new Version 2 gasket and close the joint per 5.1. With cracks: replace the casing cover (Version 2) and gasket. Do not attempt repair by welding, metal filler or liquid sealant.
6. Report the result of every inspection to Halden with the claim form, including inspections without findings. Halden uses these reports to confirm the affected population.
WARNING / WARNUNG
A cracked gasket seat can release hot liquid under pressure (up to 16 bar, 90 C). Do not approach a leaking casing joint on a running pump to re-tighten bolts. Stop and isolate the pump first.

p_79e8df3857393da815e28cdf.title: Halden HCP-350 IOM Rev D
p_79e8df3857393da815e28cdf.text_original:
WARNING Rotating shaft and coupling. Never operate the pump with the coupling guard removed.
WARNING Hot surfaces. Pump casing and bearing housings can exceed 70 C during operation. Allow to cool before maintenance.
CAUTION Dry running destroys the mechanical seal within seconds. Never start the pump unless the casing is completely filled.
NOTE Intervals apply to normal duty (clean water, up to 6,000 operating hours per year). Shorten them for contaminated liquids or continuous duty.
8.4  Replacing the mechanical seal
1. Isolate, drain and cool the pump (see 2.4). Remove the coupling guard and the coupling spacer.
2. Remove the casing bolts and withdraw the back pull-out assembly using the jacking screws.
3. Remove the impeller nut (left-hand thread) and pull off the impeller. Withdraw the seal cartridge.
4. Fit a new seal kit (18-0355). Lubricate O-rings with water or glycerine only, never with oil or grease.
5. Refit the impeller and the back pull-out assembly with a new casing gasket. Tighten the casing bolts to 45 N-m in a cross pattern, in two passes.
6. Refit the coupling spacer, re-check alignment, and refit the guard.

E-31 VFD overcurrent (VRS-110 only)
WARNING: HV-certified technicians only. The panel reset is disabled for E-31 on purpose. The reset is done under HV-PROC-07, which you can open on SharePoint if you hold the HV certification. If you don't: do not open the VFD cabinet, not even to have a look. The DC bus stays charged after the unit is isolated.
E-31 means the drive saw more current than it allows. Common reasons, in the order we see them: a grid dip or power event, a motor or motor cable fault, and occasionally an airend that's getting tight. The drive can't tell you which. The log and the conditions can.
If you're not HV-certified and you're first on site, here's what you can do , and it genuinely saves the HV tech half an hour:
Read the event log and write down every code in the hour before the trip, with times.
Note what the unit was doing: load, ambient, whether it was starting or running.
Ask the site whether there was a power event. Did anything else trip? Did lights flicker?
Photograph the controller screen and the log.
Put all of it in the case, then raise the work order with Certification required: HV (see the Work Order Writing Guide). The supervisor assigns. Don't call around to find someone yourself.
Tell the site contact the unit is out until an HV tech arrives, and roughly when. Don't promise a time you don't control.
Example of how it should go: TAC-C-0143 tripped E-31 at 04:10 on November 20, 2025 after a grid dip that also tripped half the dock lighting. Daniel came in, did the reset under HV-PROC-07, the insulation test was clean and it's been fine since. Case 00040311. Short, because the cause was obvious and written down.
If a 110 trips E-31 again soon after a reset, it's not the grid. HV-PROC-07 covers what to do with a repeat, including when to get Vastra L2 involved. Don't keep resetting it.

p_8d53a48ac5150e1416041387.title: HV-PROC-07 VRS-110 VFD Fault Reset
p_8d53a48ac5150e1416041387.text_original:
1. Purpose
This procedure tells an HV-certified technician how to investigate and clear an E-31 fault (VFD output overcurrent) on a Vastra VRS-110 rotary screw compressor and return the unit to service safely. The compressor controller will not let an E-31 be reset from the operator panel. The fault has to be cleared at the drive itself, inside the VFD cabinet, after the DC bus has been discharged and the motor has been checked.
An E-31 is usually a symptom. The drive tripped because it saw more current than it can deliver, and something caused that: a supply dip, a motor or cable insulation fault, a failing power module, or a compressor that started against load. A reset that skips the checks below can restart a compressor into a damaged motor or a failed drive, and the second trip is always more expensive than the first.
NOTE: Do not copy these steps into wiki pages, Teams chats, email or personal notes. Copies go out of date and end up with people who are not certified. Link to this document in SharePoint instead.

p_73515f8d693760063551cb19.title: HV-PROC-07 VRS-110 VFD Fault Reset
p_73515f8d693760063551cb19.text_original:
WARNING: The DC bus holds a lethal charge after the supply is isolated. The charge LED on the drive is not a safe-to-touch indication; a failed LED looks the same as a discharged bus. Only a meter reading counts.
WARNING: Arc flash. Keep the cabinet doors closed while the cabinet is energised. Wear the PPE given on the site arc flash label, and never less than the minimum in HV-PROC-02.
STOP: If you find burn marks, a smell of burnt insulation, swollen or leaking capacitors, a cracked IGBT module or melted cable insulation, stop. Do not reset. Leave the unit locked out and escalate to Vastra L2.
6. Procedure
6.1 Before isolating
Step: 1 | Action: Read the alarm log on the compressor controller. Note the time of the E-31, the load and motor speed at the time, discharge pressure, ambient temperature, and any other alarms in the 24 hours before it. | Verify / record: Photograph the alarm log screen. Enter the values in Appendix A.
Step: 2 | Action: Check the asset history in Salesforce for earlier E-31 trips and resets on this unit. | Verify / record: If an E-31 was reset on this unit in the last 24 hours, stop here and go to section 7.
Step: 3 | Action: Ask the site whether there was a power event near the time of the trip: a supply dip or outage, a generator transfer, or work in the site switchgear. | Verify / record: Record who you asked and what they said. A confirmed supply dip is the most common harmless cause.
Step: 4 | Action: Notify the site that the compressor will be isolated, normally for 60 to 90 minutes, and agree when it can go down. The site decides whether to start a standby compressor. | Verify / record: Record the name of the person notified and the agreed time.
6.2 Isolate and prove the DC bus discharged
Step: 5 | Action: Isolate the compressor at its main isolator and apply LOTO per HV-PROC-02. If the asset isolation sheet lists a separately fed control or heater supply, isolate and lock that as well. | Verify / record: Isolation permit number from HV-PROC-02 in Appendix A.
Step: 6 | Action: Wait at least 5 minutes after isolation before opening the VFD cabinet. Use the time to check the cabinet door seals and the drive cooling air inlet filter from the outside. | Verify / record: Record the time of isolation and the time the cabinet was opened.
Step: 7 | Action: Open the cabinet and remove the clear cover over the drive terminal board. Prove your CAT III meter on the proving unit. Measure TP1 to TP2, then TP1 to PE and TP2 to PE. All three readings must be below 50 V DC. Prove the meter again. | Verify / record: Record all three readings. If any reading is 50 V DC or more, refit the cover, close the cabinet, wait another 5 minutes and measure again. If the bus is still not below 50 V DC 15 minutes after isolation, stop: the discharge circuit has failed. Escalate to Vastra L2.
6.3 Inspect the drive
Step: 8 | Action: Inspect the drive with a torch: burn marks or soot, discoloured busbars, smell, cracked IGBT modules, swollen or leaking capacitors, loose or discoloured output cable lugs. Look for water or condensation on the boards. Cold store plant rooms sweat when doors are left open, and a damp drive will trip again. | Verify / record: If you find damage of any kind: STOP. Leave the LOTO in place, photograph the damage, escalate to Vastra L2 and open a High case. Do not continue with this procedure.
Step: 9 | Action: Check that the drive cooling fan turns freely by hand and that the cabinet inlet filter is clean. A blocked filter does not cause an E-31 by itself, but it shortens the life of the power modules. | Verify / record: Record the condition. Replace the filter mat if it is blocked.
6.4 Motor insulation test
Step: 10 | Action: Disconnect the motor cables from the drive output terminals U, V and W and move them clear. The drive must never see the insulation test voltage. Mark the cables so they go back in the same order. | Verify / record: Note the phase marking used.
Step: 11 | Action: Test the insulation resistance of the motor and cable at 1,000 V DC, each phase to earth, for 60 seconds per phase. Each reading must be above 100 MOhm. | Verify / record: Record the three readings. If any phase is 100 MOhm or less, do not reset. Do not try to dry the motor by running it. Go to section 7.
Step: 12 | Action: Reconnect the motor cables to U, V and W in the original order. Tighten the lugs to the torque on the label inside the cabinet door. Refit the clear cover and close the cabinet. | Verify / record: Second check of phase order by the technician before closing.
6.5 Clear the fault and test run
Step: 13 | Action: With the main isolator still locked off and the cabinet closed, switch on the 24 V auxiliary supply to the drive control board (control isolator, under your own lock control). The drive keypad on the cabinet door lights up and shows the latched overcurrent fault. | Verify / record: Fault text on the keypad matches the controller E-31.
Step: 14 | Action: On the drive keypad, set parameter P9.01 (keypad fault reset enable; some drives show it as "Rst En") to 1. Then hold RESET on the drive keypad for 3 seconds until the fault clears. P9.01 returns to 0 by itself after the reset. | Verify / record: Fault text cleared from the keypad. If it does not clear after two attempts, stop and call Vastra L2. Do not change any other drive parameter.
Step: 15 | Action: Remove the LOTO per HV-PROC-02: tools and people clear, covers fitted, cabinet doors closed and latched, then remove your locks and restore the main supply. | Verify / record: Time of re-energisation in Appendix A.
Step: 16 | Action: Start the compressor in unloaded run and let it run unloaded for 10 minutes. Watch the output current on the drive keypad for the whole run. Motor current must stay below 210 A. | Verify / record: Record the current at 1, 5 and 10 minutes, and the highest value seen. If the current reaches 210 A or the drive trips, stop, isolate and go to section 7.
Step: 17 | Action: If the unloaded run is clean, release the compressor to the site for normal operation and stay on site for at least 30 minutes of loaded running. | Verify / record: Record the loaded current and discharge temperature at the end of the 30 minutes.
Step: 18 | Action: Complete Appendix A and attach it to the Salesforce work order. Write the case resolution as FS-STD-001 section 10 requires: what you found, the readings, the likely cause, and what happens next. | Verify / record: "Reset per HV-PROC-07" on its own is not a resolution.

p_d87019c45d90f5909215147b.title: HV-PROC-07 VRS-110 VFD Fault Reset
p_d87019c45d90f5909215147b.text_original:
7. Repeat trips and decision table
Situation | Action | Decided by
First E-31 on this unit in 30 days. Supply dip confirmed by the site. Bus discharged normally, no damage, insulation above the limit. | Reset per section 6. Normal priority. Note the supply event in the case so the site can follow it up with their utility. | HV-certified technician
E-31 returns within 24 hours of a reset. | Do not reset. Leave the unit isolated. Escalate to Vastra L2 and open a High case. Inform the team lead the same day. | Technician, then supervisor
Second E-31 in 30 days but more than 24 hours after the last reset. | One reset allowed if every check in section 6 passes. Inform the team lead before the reset. The team lead decides whether to involve Vastra L2. | Team lead
Damage found at step 8 (burn marks, IGBT damage, swollen capacitors, water on boards). | Do not reset. Leave locked out. Escalate to Vastra L2. High case. | Technician
DC bus not below the limit 15 minutes after isolation. | Do not touch the terminal board. Close the cabinet, leave locked out, escalate to Vastra L2. High case. | Technician
Insulation at or below the limit on any phase. | Do not reset. Leave locked out. The motor or cable needs testing and possibly drying or replacement. Open a case for a motor test and inform the team lead. Vastra L2 if the motor is under warranty. | Team lead
Fault does not clear on the drive keypad after two attempts with P9.01 = 1. | Do not try other parameters. Leave isolated and call Vastra L2. | Vastra L2
Current reaches the limit or the drive trips during the unloaded run. | Stop, isolate, do not reset again. Escalate to Vastra L2. High case. | Technician
A different E-3x code appears after the reset. | Follow the VFD chapter of the VRS-110 service manual for that code. Treat it as a repeat trip for escalation purposes. | Technician, team lead

p_646b217d40f82e8b79a9422e.title: HV-PROC-02 Electrical Isolation Verification
p_646b217d40f82e8b79a9422e.text_original:
WARNING: Drawings and labels are often wrong. A circuit is dead when you have proved it dead at the point of work, and not before.
WARNING: Variable speed drives, capacitor banks and UPS units store energy after isolation. A motor turned by the process (a pump spun by back-flow, a fan turned by wind) generates voltage at its terminals. Treat both as live until proved otherwise.
6. Procedure
6.1 Plan the isolation
1. Read the work order and the equipment procedure. Note the required certification and any site permit.
2. Get the isolation sheet for the asset from the asset record in Salesforce. It lists every supply to the equipment. Several sites have control, heater or fan circuits fed from a different panel than the main power. If there is no isolation sheet, make one from the drawings and a walk-down, and send it to your team lead after the job.
3. Walk the route from the equipment back to each isolation point. Confirm labels against what you see.
4. Agree the isolation with the site: who is affected, for how long, and whether a standby unit is needed.
6.2 Permit
Every isolation is recorded on the isolation record in Appendix A. The record number is the Salesforce work order number followed by -E1, -E2 and so on for each isolation on that work order. Where the site runs its own permit-to-work system, get the site permit as well. The stricter rule of the two applies.
In the Netherlands the work is also registered with the site electrical responsible before isolation, as NEN 3140 requires. The Kyltek werkvergunning form is no longer used; Appendix A replaces it.
6.3 Isolate and lock
5. Stop the equipment with its normal stop control so that it shuts down in a controlled way.
6. Open each isolation point. Where you can see the contacts or the withdrawn breaker, check them visually.
7. Lock each isolation point with your personal lock and attach a tag with your name, the date, the work order number and a phone number. Where more than one person will work, lock the isolation points with the site or Corvane lock set, put the keys in the group lock box, and have each person apply a personal lock to the box.
8. Remove fuses only where the isolation sheet says so, and keep them in your possession or locked in the carrier.
6.4 Dissipate stored energy
Wait for stored energy to dissipate before opening any enclosure. For VFDs the minimum waiting time is printed on the drive label and stated in the equipment procedure. Never shorten it. Where the equipment procedure gives a DC bus test point and a value, follow it in addition to section 6.5.
Stop rotating machinery from turning before opening a motor terminal box: close the pump discharge valve to stop back-flow, or lock the fan.
6.5 Prove-test-prove
9. Use a two-pole voltage tester or a multimeter rated CAT III for the circuit voltage, in calibration, with leads and probes in good condition. Non-contact voltage detectors are not acceptable for this test.
10. Prove the tester on a proving unit or a known live source of similar voltage.
11. At the point of work, test between every pair of phases, between each phase and neutral, and between each phase and earth. On DC circuits test plus to minus and each pole to earth.
12. Prove the tester again on the same proving unit or source.
13. Record the readings in Appendix A. If the tester fails either proving, the test does not count: replace the tester and start again.
6.6 Temporary earths
Temporary earths are not needed for most work on Corvane equipment, which is fed from a single source through a short cable. Apply them when:
the conductors could be re-energised from more than one direction, for example a motor fed from a drive with a bypass contactor;
the conductors run in parallel with live circuits over a long distance (induced voltage);
the work will expose bare conductors for more than one shift; or
the site rules require them.
Apply earths only after the absence of voltage has been proved, with a device rated for the fault level at that point. Connect to earth first, then to the conductors. Remove in the reverse order. Count the earths on and off in Appendix A.
6.7 Try
Where the equipment procedure allows it, try to start the equipment from its local control after testing. Nothing should happen. Return the control to off. Do not do this on VFD-fed equipment unless the equipment procedure says so, because a start command to a drive with a fault can change its fault memory.
6.8 During the work
Your lock stays on until you have finished. If you leave site, even overnight, the lock stays on and the tag stays readable.
At a shift handover, the incoming technician applies their lock before the outgoing technician removes theirs. The isolation record is signed by both.
If the work changes so that a different circuit is exposed, stop and repeat sections 6.1 to 6.5 for that circuit.
6.9 Removal and re-energisation
14. Check that the work is complete, tools and materials are removed, covers and guards are refitted, and all temporary earths are removed and counted.
15. Tell everyone who worked on the equipment, and the site, that it will be re-energised.
16. Each person removes their own personal lock. The last person removes the isolation point locks.
17. Close the isolation points and confirm the equipment starts and runs normally.
18. Close the isolation record with the time of re-energisation.

p_f9e1145adeb8724d448f344a.title: Vastra VRS-110 Service Manual Rev A
p_f9e1145adeb8724d448f344a.text_original:
7.5 E-31 VFD overcurrent and E-36 Earth fault
The drive switches off the output immediately when the output current exceeds its peak current limit (E-31) or when it detects an earth fault current in the motor circuit (E-36). Possible causes of E-31 are a short circuit or an insulation fault in the motor or the motor cable, a blocked or heavy running element, a fault in the inverter, and supply disturbances (voltage dips) during operation at high speed. E-36 is caused by an insulation fault in the motor, the motor cable or the terminal box, often after humidity or condensate in the terminal box.
E-31 and E-36 cannot be acknowledged from the control panel or by remote reset. The Reset key has no effect while these codes are active. Reset requires access to the drive cabinet and must be carried out by an electrically qualified person authorised for work on the drive (see 7.3), after the cause has been investigated.
Before the authorised person arrives, the service technician or the operator can save time by noting from the event log the motor speed, the motor current and the DC bus voltage at the moment of the fault, by asking the site whether there was a power disturbance, and by controlling from outside that the element is not blocked (no unusual noise before the trip, no oil on the floor). Do not try to restart the compressor by switching the main isolator off and on; this does not reset the fault and stresses the drive.
NOTE If E-31 or E-36 occurs repeatedly, the compressor shall not be reset again before Vastra Technical Support has been contacted. Send the event log export and the measured values.

p_744d2fe2f13c4c270bf107bf.title: Vastra VRS-110 Service Manual Rev A
p_744d2fe2f13c4c270bf107bf.text_original:
DANGER Indicates a hazardous situation that, if not avoided, will result in death or serious injury.
WARNING Indicates a hazardous situation that, if not avoided, could result in death or serious injury.
CAUTION Indicates a situation that, if not avoided, could result in minor injury or damage to the compressor.
NOTE Gives information that is important for correct maintenance. Observe the note.
WARNING Observe that the stop key alone does not make the compressor safe. In automatic mode, and after a power failure with auto restart activated, the compressor starts without warning. Always lock the main isolator.
6.3 Fault finding procedures
6.3.1 E-13 and E-14 Discharge temperature
The controller stops the compressor when TS-2 measures more than 110 C at the element outlet (E-14). The pre-warning E-13 is shown at 105 C. On the VRS-110 a high discharge temperature appears first at full speed, which is when the cooling load is highest. Control in this order:
1 The ventilation of the compressor room and the ambient temperature (3.1). With ambient above 40 C the margin to E-14 at full speed is small. Control that hot cooling air is not recirculated and that the duct fan runs.
2 The coolers and the pre-filter mats. Clean them (5.6).
3 The oil level. Top up with Vastra SynLube 46 and look for oil leaks.
4 The cooling fan. The fan speed is controlled by the Vcon 4; control in Measurements that the fan speed reaches 100% when the discharge temperature is above 95 C.
5 The thermostatic valve. If the oil cooler stays cold while the discharge temperature is high, replace the insert.
6 The oil filter and the age of the oil.
7 The sensor TS-2. A TS-2 that reads too high gives E-14 although the compressor is not hot. With the compressor running loaded at full speed for at least 15 minutes, compare the TS-2 reading on the controller (Measurements > Discharge temperature) with a calibrated handheld contact thermometer at the discharge flange of the element. The handheld normally reads a few degrees lower, because it measures the flange surface. A difference above 8 C indicates a failing sensor: replace TS-2 (41-2207) according to 5.8.
After an E-14 shutdown, let the compressor cool for at least 15 minutes before restart. If E-14 comes back and no cause is found, export the event log and contact Vastra Technical Support. Do not raise the shutdown limit; it is fixed in the firmware.
6.3.2 E-11 Net pressure high
On the VRS-110 the pressure is regulated by the speed, and E-11 normally means that the compressor could not unload in time. Control the PT-2 reading against a reference gauge, the setpoint C1.10, the loading solenoid valve and the inlet valve. A sudden drop of the air demand to zero with a small receiver can give E-11 at full speed; the receiver volume shall be at least 1.5 m3 for the VRS-110.
6.3.3 E-09 Internal pressure low
The internal pressure does not reach 2.5 bar after loading. Control the inlet valve and its solenoid, the blow-off valve, the minimum pressure valve and the oil level. At start against an empty network the minimum pressure valve shall keep PT-1 above 4 bar; if it does not, replace the valve kit.
6.3.4 The pressure is unstable or the speed hunts
Control that PT-2 is not mounted after a filter or a dryer with a high pressure drop, that the receiver volume is sufficient, and that no other compressor on the network regulates in the same pressure band. The PI parameters shall only be changed after consultation with Vastra Technical Support.
6.3.5 The compressor does not start after a power failure
The compressor only starts by itself after a power failure if C1.05 is set to On; the restart delay C1.06 must pass first. A drive fault that occurred at the moment of the power failure must be reset before the compressor can start; see 7.4 for which faults can be reset from the control panel.

p_3b4fd549a8af2a9d2e6afb4b.title: Compressor Troubleshooting Playbook
p_3b4fd549a8af2a9d2e6afb4b.text_original:
Is the reading real (TS-2 check)
With the unit running loaded and settled, read the discharge temperature on the controller (that's TS-2) and measure the discharge flange with a calibrated contact thermometer. Use a contact probe, not the IR gun. The paint on the flange throws the IR reading off by several degrees and you'll fool yourself. If the two readings are more than 8 C apart, the sensor is suspect. The check is written up in the E-14 section of the VRS-110 manual and it works the same way on the 45 and the 75.
TS-2 is part 41-2207, same part across the whole VRS series. Keep one in the van.

On 2024-01-15 and 2025-01-20, RTM-H-0007 had L-03 on circuit 2 shortly after a winter-stop restart, it cleared after a reset/restart, and no action was taken (Servio records 2400209 and 2500253).
On 2026-02-24, case 00041055 found L-03 on circuit 2 after winter restart with suction at 2.1 bar, no leak was found visually, and the circuit was topped up with 2.5 kg R-513A and monitored.

On 2026-09-28, case 00044102 found L-03 again on circuit 2 with suction at 1.9 bar, circuit 1 normal, no oil traces visible, and no gauges connected because the tech was not F-gas certified; the unit was left running on circuit 1 only and a certified tech was needed.

The likely cause is a sticking EXV-2 rev 2 on circuit 2, because the bulletin says this fault often appears after long idle periods and the alarm can come back days or weeks later even when charge looks normal.

1. Order two valve assemblies 63-1180 (rev 3) and two filter drier cores 63-0410 per unit. Each 63-1180 kit includes the new stepper cable and a campaign label.
2. Stop the unit, isolate it electrically and lock it out.
3. Recover the refrigerant from circuit 1 into a recovery cylinder. Weigh and record the amount recovered.
4. Remove the EXV-2 rev 2 (63-1170). Braze the new valve 63-1180 in place with a nitrogen purge through the circuit. Wrap the valve body in a wet cloth; the body must not exceed 120 C.
5. Replace the filter drier core with 63-0410.
6. Pressure test and evacuate the circuit as described in the NK-600 Service Manual and according to local regulations.
7. Charge by weight to the nameplate charge of the circuit. If refrigerant was added to this circuit at an earlier visit for an L-03 alarm, do not return the recovered amount blindly: the nameplate charge is the target.
8. Fit the new stepper cable. The rev 2 cable does not fit the rev 3 motor and must not be modified.
9. In Service > Configuration > Circuit 1 > EXV type, select "rev 3". With the wrong setting the valve opens too slowly.
10. Repeat steps 3 to 9 for circuit 2.
11. Start the unit. After 30 minutes check on both circuits that the EXV position follows the request and that superheat is stable.
12. Fit the campaign label next to the nameplate. Log the work and the refrigerant quantities in the unit's F-gas record.
13. Return the two removed valves to Nordkyl within 30 days with the return label from the partner portal. The returned valves are part of the claim.

p_7b4109a82f1f5490d4cc98d5.title: Nordkyl SB-2025-014
p_7b4109a82f1f5490d4cc98d5.text_original:
· The alarm often clears after a reset and a restart and comes back days or weeks later. This is why units have been topped up in the field without a leak being found.
ROOT CAUSE
The needle of the EXV-2 rev 2 runs in a PTFE guide bushing. During long idle periods at low temperature, a thin film from the POE compressor oil forms between needle and bushing. The stepper motor of rev 2 runs with a low holding current, and at start it does not always have the torque to break the needle free. The motor loses steps and the needle stays at a small opening while the controller asks for more.
The position feedback of the valve reports the real needle position, so the condition can be seen in the service menu. EXV-2 rev 3 (63-1180) has a coated needle without the PTFE bushing and a stronger stepper motor. It has not shown the fault in 18 months of field operation or in cold-soak tests at Nordkyl Aarhus.
DIAGNOSIS: CHECK THE EXV BEFORE LEAK TESTING OR CHARGING

p_d825d520c28e9682a85fcc94.title: Nordkyl SB-2025-014
p_d825d520c28e9682a85fcc94.text_original:
1. Confirm that the unit serial number is in the range above.
2. Let the alarmed circuit run, or restart it, for at least 10 minutes.
3. On the controller, open Service > Circuits > Circuit 1 (or 2) > EXV. Read "EXV request" and "EXV position" in %. Service level login is needed.
4. If the position stays below 15% while the request is higher (usually 40 to 100%), the valve is stuck. The fault is confirmed. Do not add refrigerant. Replace the valves as described below.
5. If the position follows the request within about 5%, the EXV is not the cause of this alarm. Continue with the L-03 troubleshooting in the NK-600 Service Manual. The unit is still in the campaign; schedule the valve replacement.
6. Do not tap the valve body to free it. A valve that moves after tapping is still defective and will stick again.
Write down the request and position values for both circuits. They are needed for the campaign claim.
CORRECTIVE ACTION: REPLACE EXV-2 ON BOTH CIRCUITS
Replace the valve on both circuits of the unit, also when only one circuit has alarmed. The work opens the refrigerant circuit and may only be done by refrigerant-certified technicians (EU F-gas Category I or national equivalent). Allow half a day on site for the unit.

p_9487c3add93b074b3663bf5c.text_original:
FIELD CAMPAIGN  NK-C25-14 NK-600: expansion valve EXV-2 rev 2 can stick partly closed after idle periods
Bulletin
Category
Issued SB-2025-014 Reliability, field campaign 2 September 2025
Campaign code Product
Revision NK-C25-14 NK-600 air-cooled chiller, R-513A 0
 | Before you leak test or add refrigerant On an NK-600 in the serial range below with an L-03 alarm, check the EXV position in the service menu first (section 4). A sticking expansion valve starves the evaporator and gives the same alarm as a low charge. Adding refrigerant does not correct it, and the circuit is overcharged when the valve frees again.
AFFECTED UNITS
Model | Serial numbers | Market | Valve fitted | Status
NK-600 | NK600-220001 to NK600-231999 | EU deliveries | EXV-2 rev 2 (63-1170) | In campaign NK-C25-14
NK-600 | NK600-220001 to NK600-231999 | Outside EU | Other valve supplier | Not affected
NK-600 | NK600-232000 and later | All | EXV-2 rev 3 (63-1180) | Not affected
NK-300 | All | All | EXV-1 | Not affected
The list of serial numbers in the campaign, with completion status, is available to authorised partners in the Nordkyl partner portal under Campaigns. The rev 2 valve can also be recognised on the unit: its stepper motor has a grey cable with a 4-pin connector; the rev 3 motor has a black cable with a 6-pin connector.
SYMPTOM
· Alarm L-03 (low suction pressure) on one circuit only. The other circuit runs normally.
· Typically in the first hours after a restart that follows an idle period of more than 48 hours: weekend shutdown, low load in winter, or after maintenance. More frequent at low ambient temperature.
· Refrigerant charge is normal: liquid line sight glass clear, subcooling in the normal range, no leak found.
· Suction superheat on the affected circuit is high, while the controller log shows the EXV request rising toward 100%.

p_03703ad7cbd514fafba64c98.title: SOP-020 Chiller Leak Test and Refrigerant Recharge
p_03703ad7cbd514fafba64c98.text_original:
WARNING: Refrigerant can cause frostbite and, in enclosed spaces, asphyxiation. Wear safety glasses and cryogenic gloves when connecting hoses. Ventilate plant rooms before work. R-513A is classified A1 (non-flammable), but its decomposition products near open flames or hot surfaces are toxic.
STOP: Never top up a circuit to clear a low suction pressure alarm. If you cannot find the cause, stop and escalate.
6. Procedure
6.1 Before you connect gauges
1. Check the asset's serial number against open service bulletins and campaigns for the model. On Nordkyl NK-600 units covered by the EXV replacement campaign, follow the bulletin first: a sticking expansion valve produces the same alarm as a low charge.
2. Read the alarm history on the controller. Note which circuit alarmed, when, and the suction and discharge pressures at the time.
3. Check for causes that are not a leak: an iced evaporator, low chilled water flow, a dirty condenser coil, a blocked filter drier (temperature drop across the drier above 3 C), or an expansion valve not modulating.
4. Inspect for oil stains at joints, flare nuts, service valves and the compressor. Oil marks the place where refrigerant escapes.
6.2 Leak test
5. Run the unit and leak test both circuits with a calibrated electronic leak detector (sensitivity 3 g/year or better). Move the probe at no more than 5 cm per second, below joints, because R-513A is heavier than air.
6. Confirm every indication with bubble solution before opening the circuit.
7. If no leak is found but the charge is low, do not top up. Record the result, tag the unit, and escalate to the team lead for an ultrasonic or tracer-gas test. A charge that disappeared went somewhere.
6.3 Repair and pressure test
8. Recover the refrigerant from the affected circuit into a labelled recovery cylinder. Weigh and record the recovered amount.
9. Repair the leak. Replace the filter drier (part 63-0410) whenever the circuit has been opened.
10. Fit the gauge manifold and nitrogen regulator. Never pressurise directly from the nitrogen cylinder without a regulator.
11. Pressurise in steps: 3 bar, check for audible leaks; 10 bar, check with bubble solution.
12. Pressurize with dry nitrogen to 15 bar, hold for 30 minutes, and assess the result against the acceptance criteria in Appendix C. Record the start and end pressure and the ambient temperature at start and end, because nitrogen pressure changes with temperature.
13. Release the nitrogen to atmosphere outdoors.
6.4 Evacuation
14. Connect a vacuum pump with short, large-bore hoses and remove the Schrader cores for faster evacuation.
15. Evacuate to below 500 microns.
16. Isolate the pump and hold for 15 minutes. If the vacuum rises above 1,000 microns, there is moisture or a leak: return to 6.3.
6.5 Charging
17. Charge by weight to the nameplate charge of the circuit, as liquid, through the liquid line service valve.
18. Start the circuit and check suction pressure, discharge pressure, superheat and subcooling against the values in the manufacturer's manual.
19. Leak test the repaired joint again with the unit running.
20. Label the unit with the refrigerant type, the total charge and the date.
NOTE: In the EU, units with a charge of 5 t CO2-equivalent or more need periodic leak checks by law. For R-513A (GWP 631) that is any circuit above 7.9 kg. Every NK-600 and NK-300 qualifies.

p_3e4df73910f64523fd1acff3.title: Nordkyl NK-600 Service Manual Rev C
p_3e4df73910f64523fd1acff3.text_original:
6.3 Diagnosing L-03
L-03 is the most frequent alarm on air-cooled chillers and the one most often misdiagnosed. Low suction pressure means the evaporator is getting too little refrigerant, or is taking up too little heat. A low charge is only one of the causes. An EXV that does not open as far as the controller commands starves the evaporator in exactly the same way, and produces the same alarm.
Before connecting gauges, open the EXV menu for the alarmed circuit and the alarm log entry. Then compare:
Reading | Low charge (leak) | EXV restricted or not opening | Blocked filter drier | Iced evaporator / low flow
Superheat | High | High | High | Low or normal
EXV position shown | At or near 100 % | Any value; often normal | At or near 100 % | Low
Subcooling | Low (below 2 K) | Normal or high | Normal before the drier | Normal
Sight glass | Bubbles | Clear | Bubbles after the drier | Clear
Temperature drop across FD1 | Below 1 K | Below 1 K | Above 3 K | Below 1 K
The EXV position shown on the display is calculated from the number of steps the driver has sent. It is not measured at the valve. A valve that is sticking reports a normal position while passing far less refrigerant than the position suggests. Use the manual test in 7.4.3 to check whether the valve actually responds.
IMPORTANT Do not add refrigerant to clear L-03. If the charge is low, there is a leak: find and repair it first (chapter 8). Adding refrigerant to a circuit with a restricted EXV floods the condenser, raises the discharge pressure, and in warm weather leads to L-01.

from: Sofie de Vries <s.devries@corvane.eu>; sent: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 05:48:09 +0000; to: Lena Hoffmann <l.hoffmann@corvane.eu>; subject: RE: FW: RTM-H-0007 alarm again - second visit this year

Hoi Lena,

As promised on the phone last night, here it is in writing so you have it for Pieter and for the file. Sorry it didn't make 15:00 yesterday, I was on a roof in Botlek with no signal most of the afternoon.

February first, because you asked and because it was my visit.

I did the February call-out (00041055). L-03 on circuit 2 after the winter restart, suction 2.1 bar. I worked to KT-WI-14: visual inspection of circuit 2, the joints, service valves and around the compressor, no oil traces, no leak found. The deficit came out under 10% of nameplate charge, so per KT-WI-14 I topped up 2.5 kg R-513A and left it running to monitor. That is what the work instruction says, and it's how we did it at Kyltek for years. KT-WI-14 also says to schedule a full leak test at the next planned visit. I can't find in Servio or Salesforce that it was ever scheduled. I should have made sure it was.

What I didn't do: I did not check the EXV campaign. RTM-H-0007 is serial NK600-230415. That is inside the serial range of the Nordkyl bulletin SB-2025-014 (NK600-220001 up to NK600-231999), campaign NK-C25-14. The symptom in the bulletin is L-03 after idle periods with normal charge, because the expansion valve sticks. A winter restart is exactly an idle period. So your memory is right, and it is quite possible the February alarm was the valve and not the charge at all, and I put 2.5 kg into a circuit that didn't need it. I'll check for that too.

Eerlijk gezegd, the worst part is that I put the campaign warning on the EU chiller field guide myself last October. I didn't connect it on the day. Balen.

I've checked what we have. No record of the campaign being done on 0007. RTM-H-0008 is NK600-240702, outside the range, so that one is fine. GDN-H-0014 in Gdansk is NK600-221190, also inside the range, but that one Jakub and I did last October. That is the unit that taught us about the valve in the first place, which makes missing it on 0007 worse.

Who goes: me. Jakub can't, he isn't F-gas certified yet, and he did the right thing on Monday by not putting gauges on it. I can be on site Thursday 1 October at 07:00. Jakub has asked Pieter's shift lead for roof access and the work at height permit for Thursday morning. I'll take Jakub with me so he sees it done.

Plan on site:
1. Check the EXV on circuit 2 first, before anything is connected to the refrigerant side: valve position in the service menu at restart and under load, superheat, and whether it's modulating or stuck. Also check which valve is fitted, rev 2 or rev 3. The label is readable on that unit.
2. If it's the valve: replace with 63-1180 rev 3 on both circuits as the campaign says, booked under NK-C25-14. I emailed Mette Kjaer at Nordkyl this morning to confirm 0007 is still open on their campaign list and to get two valves sent to Rotterdam. If they're not here by Thursday, I do the diagnosis Thursday and come back for the swap.
3. If the valve is fine, or the charge is still short after the valve: leak test per SOP-020 and repair. No top-up. If I can't find the leak, I tag the unit and escalate, which is what SOP-020 says to do.

cases.question: Just put a new belt on a BX-12 and it keeps tracking left. I've adjusted the take-up a few times. Any known fix?

segments.text: Yes — for BX-12 units built in 2023 and 2024, a known cause of a new belt tracking left after take-up adjustment is a return idler from production lot 23-11 with an off-centre bore; the fix is to replace that return idler with part 77-0419.
This applies only to BX-12 built in 2023 and 2024; if you keep chasing the take-up instead of replacing the idler, the belt will keep steering left and you can hide the real fault.
Isolate and lock off the BCU-2 before you replace the return idler.
Slacken both take-up screws by two turns, remove the return idler, fit 77-0419, and make sure it turns freely and runs true.

Re-tension the belt evenly, then re-check tracking after three belt revolutions; the interim fix from Belton is to keep both take-up screws even and shim the tail pulley bearing on the drive side by 0.5 mm until the idler is changed.
Corvane case 00041750 and MaintPro record 229186 show the same fault on FRS-V-0201, and the completed repair was a 77-0419 idler replacement with tracking OK afterward.

p_82ab900842586b83c90077df.title: RE: BX-12 tracking after belt change
p_82ab900842586b83c90077df.text_original:
from: Henrik Sauer <h.sauer@belton-conveyors.co.uk>; sent: Mon, 11 May 2026 08:14:22 +0000; to: Olu Adeyemi <o.adeyemi@corvane.com>; cc: Tom Becker <t.becker@corvane.com>; subject: RE: BX-12 tracking after belt change

CAUTION: This email originated from outside of Corvane Field Services. Do not click links or open attachments unless you recognize the sender and know the content is safe.

Morning Olu, Tom,

Thanks for the photos and the lot number, that confirms it. And the wobble you saw is real, it's not your eyes.

Return idlers from production lot 23-11 have an off-centre bore. It was a machining problem at our roller supplier. We caught it in early 2025, but by then the lot had gone out on new machines and as spares. The roller runs very slightly eccentric, which is enough to steer the return side of the belt. On a belt that's been running a while you often don't see it, because the old belt has taken a set and its edges have worn in. Put a new belt on and it follows the idler. The belt walks to the drive side every time, which is exactly what you've got.

The fix is to replace that return idler with the revised part, 77-0419. Same roller, corrected bore, and it has a blue end cap instead of black so you can tell them apart on the frame. It isn't in the parts list of your Rev B manual. Quote 77-0419 to the distributor and they'll find it, or I can ship from Leeds. I'll send two at no charge, one for 0201 and one for 0202 (see below). Please send me a delivery address in Fresno.

Until the idler arrives, this will let them run at full speed:

1. Set both take-up screws back to equal, at the position that gives you the 0.4% you measured. Your tension was right, don't change it.
2. Shim the tail pulley bearing on the drive side by 0.5 mm. The shim goes behind the bearing block, between the block and the take-up slide, so the drive-side end of the tail pulley moves 0.5 mm back towards the tail. Use one 0.5 mm piece of stainless shim, not a stack of thin ones.
3. Run the belt and re-check the tracking after three belt revolutions. On that length at line speed that's a couple of minutes. It should settle and hold centre. If it's still walking after three revolutions, stop and ring me, because then it's something else.
4. When you fit the 77-0419, take the shim out again, set the take-up even, and re-check after three revolutions as before.

This affects BX-12 built in 2023 and 2024. Your 0202 (BX12-240078) came off the line the same week as 0201 and very likely has a 23-11 idler as well. It will show itself the day you change that belt, so I'd swap the idler at its next PM rather than wait. If you have BX-20s anywhere, they use a different idler and aren't affected.

Sorry this has cost you and the plant a week. We should have put a bulletin out on it, and we haven't. I've raised that again internally this morning.

Kind regards,

p_2ebe5e222ffde9553746cf3d.title: Belton BX-12 O&M Manual Rev B
p_2ebe5e222ffde9553746cf3d.text_original:
Belt tracking
7.1 How tracking works A belt moves towards the end of a pulley or roller that it touches first. The crowned drive and tail pulleys pull the belt towards their centre, but only if the frame is square, the pulleys are square to the frame and every roller the belt touches is free and square. Tracking on the BX-12 is adjusted at the tail pulley only. Do not move the drive pulley; it is squared at the factory.
to drive end
 |  | belt, travelling away from you |  | 
 | tail pulley |  |  | 
LEFT take-up RIGHT take-up
Figure 7-1  Tail end seen from the infeed. Belt running to the left: tighten the LEFT take-up (or slacken the right). Belt running to the right: tighten the RIGHT take-up.
7.2 Procedure Run the belt empty at the normal speed. Watch the belt at the tail pulley for at least three full revolutions of the belt before deciding which way it is going.
a) If the belt runs off to the left, tighten the left-hand take-up screw a quarter of a turn, or slacken the right-hand screw a quarter of a turn. If it runs to the right, do the opposite.
b) Wait for three revolutions of the belt. The belt reacts slowly; impatience is the commonest cause of over-correction.
c) Repeat in quarter turns until the belt runs centrally at the tail and at the drive.
d) Load the belt with typical product and check again.
e) Re-check the tension (Section 6). Tracking adjustments change it slightly.
NOTE: Make small adjustments only. If you need more than two full turns of difference between the left and right take-up screws, the cause is somewhere else and the adjustment is only hiding it.
7.3 If the belt will not track Belts that track badly after a belt change usually have one of these causes. Check them in this order:
a) Take-ups not equal. Compare the left and right screw projections with a rule.
b) Frame out of square (4.2), often after the conveyor has been moved or a leg has been knocked.
c) Product residue or wear on the pulley faces. Clean with warm water; never use solvent on the lagging.

p_5cbce5243055902e6aa24c55.title: Belton BX-12 O&M Manual Rev B
p_5cbce5243055902e6aa24c55.text_original:
Belt replacement
8.1 The BX-12 belt is endless and is replaced from the right-hand side, which has removable bed plates and a cantilevered return frame. Allow one hour for two people on a 6 m conveyor.
a) Isolate and lock off the BCU-2.
b) Remove the side guards on the right-hand side. Slacken both take-up screws fully and note their positions.
c) Remove the four bolts holding the right-hand return frame brackets and the bed plate retaining clips.
d) Slide the old belt off sideways. Inspect the slider bed for wear and grooves while it is exposed.
e) Check the direction arrow on the inside of the new belt (77-1012) and fit it with the arrow pointing towards the drive end on the top run.
f) Refit the return frame brackets (tighten to 25 Nm), the bed plate clips and the guards.
g) Tension the belt to 0.3 % (Section 6) and track it (Section 7).
h) Re-check tension and tracking after 8 hours and 50 hours of running.
8.2 Replacing a return idler Return idlers drop into slotted brackets on both side frames and are held by spring clips.
a) Isolate and lock off the BCU-2. Slacken both take-up screws by two turns each to take the weight off the idlers.
b) Remove the spring clips at both ends of the idler and lift it out of its slots.
c) Fit the new idler (77-0410). Check that both hexagon shaft ends sit fully down in their slots, and refit the clips.
d) Spin the idler by hand. It must turn freely and run true.
e) Re-tension the belt by turning both screws back two turns, then check the tension marks (Section 6) and the tracking (Section 7).
8.3 Replacing the geared motor The geared motor is mounted on the drive pulley shaft with a hollow shaft and torque arm.
a) Isolate and lock off. Unplug the motor cable at the motor.
b) Remove the torque arm bolt and the shaft end retaining bolt.
c) Draw the motor off the shaft with a puller on the extraction thread. Do not hammer on the gear housing.

p_97786b4e03a9d42b30bf8270.title: Belton BX-12 O&M Manual Rev B
p_97786b4e03a9d42b30bf8270.text_original:
Belt tensioning
6.1 The belt needs just enough tension to drive without slipping. Too little and the belt slips on the drive pulley (fault C-03). Too much and it overloads the pulley bearings, stretches the belt and makes tracking harder, not easier.
6.2 Elongation method Belton specifies tension as elongation of the belt: 0.3 - 0.5 % of its relaxed length. Measure it like this:
a) Isolate the conveyor. Slacken both take-up screws until the belt is just slack.
b) On the top run near the middle of the conveyor, mark two fine lines across the belt exactly 1000
mm apart.
c) Tighten the left and right take-up screws equally, counting the turns, until the marks are 1003 mm to 1005 mm apart (0.3 - 0.5 %).
d) Tighten the take-up lock nuts to 35 Nm.
e) Run the belt and check the tracking (Section 7).
6.3 New belts Set a new belt to 0.3 %. A new belt relaxes during running-in. Check the marks again after 8 hours and 50 hours of running and re-tension to 0.3 - 0.5 % if needed. Always turn both screws by the same amount, or you will change the tracking as well as the tension.
